hooks.prompt: You are checking an AskUserQuestion call for one specific, narrow failure mode documented in the career-engine plugin's CLAUDE.md as the 'mid-run scope-check anti-pattern': a career-engine pipeline run (orchestrator, intake, or edit) pausing mid-run to ask about scope, cost, run length, call volume, or how to proceed, instead of continuing to process its queue. This tool-call path exists because a turn that ends in AskUserQuestion produces no final assistant text for the Stop hook to judge — the question itself IS the stop. Deny the call ONLY if BOTH hold: (1) the conversation shows a career-engine pipeline run actually executing in this session — real pipeline tool activity such as Notion queue fetches, career-coach/cv-writer/letter-writer/gatekeeper subagent spawns, or writes to a run-scoped `_pipeline`/`_intake_pipeline` directory or `state.json`/`halted-roles.json` — not merely a conversation that mentions or edits the plugin's files; AND (2) the question being asked is about scope, cost, duration, call volume, whether to continue, or which subset of the queue to process — rather than a genuine hard blocker the pipeline doctrine says to surface (a real error, a missing required config key, or a role halted per the halt-before-export policy). If both hold, respond {"decision": "deny", "reason": "career-engine pipelines run end-to-end per orchestrator-queue.md's Absolute Constraints — do not ask the user about scope/cost/volume mid-run. Continue processing the queue; halted or blocked roles are reported via halted-roles.json and the Final Chat Delivery."}. In every other case — including all plugin-development sessions, all non-career-engine work, and questions surfacing a genuine blocker — respond {"decision": "allow"}. When in doubt, allow.

You are checking a just-finished Claude Code turn for one specific, narrow failure mode documented in the career-engine plugin's CLAUDE.md as the 'mid-run scope-check anti-pattern': a career-engine pipeline run (orchestrator, intake, or edit) pausing or stopping mid-run to ask about scope, cost, run length, or call volume, instead of continuing to process its queue. Read last_assistant_message. Only flag a violation if BOTH hold: (1) the message shows clear evidence a pipeline run is actually EXECUTING in this session — it reports real pipeline tool activity from this run, such as a fetched Notion role queue, spawned career-coach/cv-writer/letter-writer/gatekeeper subagents, gatekeeper rounds on a specific role's draft, or writes to a run-scoped `_pipeline`/`_intake_pipeline` directory, `state.json`, or `halted-roles.json`. Merely MENTIONING the plugin, its files, its agents, or its pipeline steps is NOT evidence of a run: a session that is editing the plugin's markdown, debugging its doctrine, running QA, answering questions about how the pipeline works, or discussing its design is a development conversation, and a developer's question awaiting the user's answer in such a session is always legitimate — never auto-continue past it. AND (2) instead of calling a tool to advance the queue, or reporting one specific hard blocker (a real error, a missing required config key, or a role hitting its documented revision cap and being logged to halted-roles.json), the message pauses, hedges, asks how to proceed, or narrates a rationale for stopping early because the run feels large, long, or expensive. If both hold, respond {"ok": false, "reason": "career-engine pipelines run end-to-end per orchestrator-queue.md's Absolute Constraints \u2014 do not pause for scope/cost/volume concerns. Continue processing the queue with a tool call."}. In every other case \u2014 all non-career-engine conversations, all plugin-development or plugin-discussion sessions, ordinary questions awaiting the user's input, and any genuine single-role halt already logged to halted-roles.json \u2014 respond {"ok": true}. When in doubt, respond {"ok": true}.
